title: Portrayal rack product (v1) - a frame or cabinet the library models
description: A RACK PRODUCT IS A RACK OR A CABINET AS A MAKER SELLS IT. It lives at racks/<vendor>/<name>/rack.yaml, is versioned by the rack.lock.json beside it, and is referenced as <vendor>/<name>@<major>. It is not a device (a device is placed in a rack; a rack is not) and it is not the Rack Builder's file (`rack.schema.json`, the rack someone built). It holds the frame (height, numbering, posts, holes and the rails) and, for a cabinet, its enclosure (doors, side panels and roof), its base and its zero-U channels. Further parts of a cabinet arrive as additive keys; until then an unknown key is refused, never ignored.

name.description: the directory name, unique within the vendor across racks AND devices, so a ref never needs the kind to resolve (L193)

version.description: semver, checked against rack.lock.json. Major: a number a saved rack file copies or positions against (height, numbering, width, holes, rail positions and depth, the depth a device may have, hole centres once stated). Minor: a figure stated where there was none (a load rating, a weight, the outer box). Patch: a statement nothing positions against (prose, provenance, a corrected rating).

maturity.description: as a device states it: draft needs nothing, modelled needs provenance citing a document, verified needs every figure read from one

manufacturer.description: the maker on the product, which is the namespace it lives under: APC's racks are under `apc` however a reseller lists them

part-numbers.description: orderable SKU -> what it is, as a device writes them

aliases.description: the other names the product is sold or listed under; one shape, as a device's aliases

form.description: the NetBox and Nautobot form slug, plus `desktop-frame`, which neither has and which exports as `2-post-frame`. It says how the rack stands and how many posts it has, so a rack has no `mount` key

ru.description: rack units the rack OFFERS (a device's `ru` is the units it takes)

direction.description: the way the labels run, by the direction the maker's text gives. A rack file stores positions bottom-up whatever this says

start.description: the label of the first unit; 1 unless the source says otherwise (NetBox `starting_unit`)

width.description: nominal rail width, inches. Absent means 19

holes.description: the hole style is a FIT FACT, not decoration: a part that clips into holes refuses a tapped rail

thread.description: the thread of a tapped hole, and only of one

size.description: mm across a square or round hole, written only where a source prints it

fixing.description: what a square or round hole takes (`M6` cage nuts), written only where a source says

hole-centres.description: mm from the left hole line to the right. Written where a source prints it, or as an EIA-310 stand-in that `provenance` and `gaps` declare

opening.description: mm clear between the rails, with the same rule as `hole-centres`

rails.description: the rail planes: `front`, and on a four-post frame `rear`. L193 holds the list to the form

depth.description: mm from the front rail to this one, fixed or a range the Rack Builder sets within

max-device-depth.description: mm, the maker's usable depth (the rack file's `usableDepth`)

outer.description: the outside box in mm, width, height and depth, as the maker prints it

weight-kg.description: the rack's own weight, written only where a source gives it

load.description: the maker's ratings. A rating not stated is not written; the catalogue says `not stated`, never zero

enclosure.description: what closes a cabinet in: its doors, its side panels and its roof. Only a cabinet form has one (L193); an open frame has none. Each part is written only where a document states it

doors.description: the doors of the cabinet, one entry for each face that has any

face.description: the face of the cabinet the door closes, once each (L193)

leaves.description: how many separate leaves the door is: 2 is a split pair that opens from the middle

kind.description: what the leaf is made of: a perforated or mesh leaf lets air through, a solid or glass one does not

open-area.description: the percentage of a perforated or mesh leaf that is open, as the maker prints it. It says how much air the door passes

hinge.description: the side the hinges are on as the door ships, seen from the face. A split pair states none

reversible.description: true when the maker says the hinges and the latch can be swapped to the other side. Needs a `hinge` to say which side it ships on (L193)

swing.description: degrees the door opens to, as the maker prints it. A viewer that draws the door open turns it by this much

clearance.description: mm of wiring space between the door and the vertical rail behind it. A device whose face stands proud of the rail by more than this would stop the door closing

lock.description: how the door is locked: `key` is a handle that locks with a key

panels.description: the panels that close each long side of the cabinet

per-side.description: how many panels close one side

split.description: how a side with two panels is divided: `top-bottom` is an upper and a lower panel

removable.description: true when a panel can be taken off without taking the cabinet apart

lock.description: how a panel is locked: `key` is a lock that takes a key

roof.description: the roof panel of the cabinet

removable.description: true when the roof comes off without tools or without taking the cabinet apart, as the maker says

base.description: what the cabinet stands on. Each count is written only where a document states it

casters.description: how many casters the cabinet rolls on

levellers.description: how many adjustable levelling feet it stands on once in place

channels.description: the zero-U channels inside the cabinet: vertical strips beside the rails that a rack PDU or a cable accessory hangs from. A rack file names the channel a part stands in by its `id`, so a part in a channel and one outside the cabinet never meet

id.description: the channel's name, unique within the product (L193). A saved rack names the channel by it, so it is never reused for another channel

point.description: the zero-U attachment point the channel belongs to, one the form has: `left` and `right` on a two-post frame, the four corner points on a four-post one (L193)

where.description: `inside` is between the posts, behind the side panel; `outside` is against the outer face of an upright

slots.description: the column of slots a hanging part's mounting buttons enter. `first`, `pitch` and `count` are stated together or not at all

interface.description: the mount the slots present, a key of the connector registry (L193): `pdu-button` is the keyhole that takes the shoulder button on the back of a zero-U PDU

first.description: mm from the bottom of the rails to the first slot

pitch.description: mm from one slot to the next, up the channel

count.description: how many slots the column has

moves.description: the ways the maker says the channel can be moved from where it ships

front-back.description: true when the channel slides forward and back along the side rails

datasheet.description: the product data sheet, as a device registers it

references.description: the other documents the figures came from. A `sha256` is present exactly when the project holds a copy

provenance.description: where each figure came from, keyed by the rack's own key (L193). `confidence` is the library's word for it; a figure no document prints is `estimated`, and is also a `gaps` entry

gaps.description: what the sources do not say, as a device declares it: a token, why it is missing, and what would close it
